summary: George Lakoff is a scholar in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1958–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966), and later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Loyola University Maryland (~1887–1891) and Johns Hopkins University (~1891–1896), he held posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).

George Peiris Malalasekera worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids and William Stede. He held posts at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

George Roerich worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Lobsang Mingyur Dorje and attended the University of London and Harvard University, later serving at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1957–1960).

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard College, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Harvard University, completing his doctorate under William James (~1886–1889). He held an academic post at Harvard University from ~1889 to 1912.
George Sessions was a scholar in the field of philosophy. He held posts at Sierra College in 1992–1993 and in 2002.
George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

George Thibaut worked in Indology and studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1879–1888), Principal at Muir Central College (~1895–1906), and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1907–1914).
George Watt studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1868–1871) and the University of Glasgow (~1871–1873). He later held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from ~1873 to 1884.

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University (~1983–1987). He held posts at Leiden University (~1987–2009), the University of Bern (2010–2022), and the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (2020).

Georges Dreyfus works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding posts at the University of Virginia (~1991–1992) and Williams College (~1992).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure in 1974, he held posts at Blaise Pascal University (~1993–2002) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1999).

Georgios T. Halkias specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and held posts at SOAS (~2008–2011), Ruhr University Bochum (~2011–2013), and the University of Hong Kong (~2014).

Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later holding posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1970–1995) and Indiana University (~1995–2003).

Gereon Kopf works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University, was mentored by Yasuo Yuasa, and held posts at J. F. Oberlin University, Luther College, the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford, supervised by Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Innsbruck, studied under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, and held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (from 1964).

Geshe Gendun Lodro worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Khensur Ngawang Lekden at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (~1947–1961). He held positions at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).
